title: Drift & Coherence Review (trend vs 2026-11-04): a very quiet window (8 LinearViewer + 8 SD commits, the records-first cost cutover and the runner's snapshot-path removal) - verify the 11-04 ledger and open items, the usage-relay flag after LIN-4203, and the usage-records wire across LinearViewer + simple-dispatcher + the runner kit
description:
<!-- harbour-periodical-gate id="drift-coherence-review" -->

**Drift & Coherence Review** is the trend-aware periodical (`drift-coherence` in `lib/periodicals.js`, series anchor LIN-369). It looks for code that is locally right while the system as a whole drifts apart. **This task is the review itself.** You write the report, mint the highest-severity follow-ups, get an adversarial second-read, merge the report PR, and then conclude this task. Assume a cold hand-off: all you have is this description plus access to the repos and Linear.

This run is also read as the **top-down reading for the Survey research** (`docs/plans/survey/log.md` and `docs/plans/survey/place-ledger.md` on branch `claude/cool-rubin-6acj5j`). That is context for what the numbers are used for, not extra scope: do not edit anything on that branch, and do not change what you report to fit it. If a finding bears on a place named in the place ledger, say so in one line and cross-link.

**Repos in remit:** `JKershaw/LinearViewer` (Harbour, primary), `JKershaw/simple-dispatcher` (SD), and the runner kit inside Harbour (`lib/runner-kit/`, `docs/runner-prompt.md`). The cross-repo contract between them (runner contract table, halt, markers, consumer heartbeat, the model/effort/harness vocabulary, and the per-request usage records) is a seam no sibling review owns, so it belongs to this review.

**This is a very quiet window, and that is a valid outcome.** The previous edition (`docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-04.md`, LIN-4209, Done, PR #2271, merge `f5bc752c`) was written about ten hours before this task was minted, and it was itself a delta against the 11-03 edition. The window since its measured commits is 8 LinearViewer commits (4 of them docs-only reports) and 8 SD commits (see Grounding). A short, mostly "unchanged / held" report is the expected shape; a near-empty delta is a genuine result. Do not widen the window, invent make-work, re-flag the 11-04 ledger as new, or pad the report to look like the previous edition. What a small window does change: the report's value is (a) a trustworthy "unchanged / touched but not consolidated / resolved" reading of the 11-04 ledger (121 rows), (b) a close read of the few things that did move, and (c) a second look at the items the 11-04 run left open. Say plainly in the report how small the window was and what that did to the confidence of each "unchanged".

---

## Grounding (as found at mint time, 2026-11-04 \~18:00Z). Re-verify all of it; nothing here is a finding.

All numbers below are pre-mint probes from the minting agent. **Verify, don't quote.** Re-measure at your own HEAD and say if HEAD moved.

* **HEADs at mint.** LinearViewer `origin/main` = `d7ceb373444f9efbc027656132352d247535aa5e` (LIN-4203, #2274, 17:18Z). simple-dispatcher `origin/main` = `d8d186c07113d6e61e3489e38f1210d0b0624cad` (LIN-4187, #324, 17:44Z).
* **The previous edition measured:** LinearViewer `5334c81a7207b9f2cc85ca429a2c6b18e1635c0e` and SD `502901c3e9a36b90eeafd95f23b59f35ef80c195` (mint was `67ff5c3`; one test-and-docs commit landed after). The 11-03 edition measured `015aa4c6` / `cf6369d`.
* **The window.**
  * LinearViewer `5334c81a..d7ceb373`: **8 commits**. Four are docs-only (`e439f637` Seams run 5, `1403d52d` Code Quality, `57b22b92` Stability, `f5bc752c` the 11-04 Drift report). Four are code: LIN-4200 (`230cc2c2`, two measurement scripts), LIN-4212 (`eb44eff9`, request records read by posting row), LIN-4201 (`2ee4e600`, the cost read sums request records; records-first cutover, LIN-4195 piece 4) and LIN-4203 (`d7ceb373`, the runner kit stops posting `[usage]`; intake counts legacy snapshots). Production (`lib routes public server.js`): **33 files, +1,049 / -288**. **Added:** `lib/request-usage-fold.js`, `request-usage-loader.js`, `request-usage-vocabulary.js`, `usage-snapshot-intake.js`, `workspace-kpis-cache.js`. **Deleted:** `lib/founder-lookup.js`. The runner kit changed in `lib/runner-kit/runner.mjs` (+74/-), `docs/runner-prompt.md` (13 lines); `lib/runner-kit/contract.json` did not change. `scripts/code-shape/areas.json` was edited (LIN-4201, placement only).
  * SD `502901c..d8d186c`: **8 commits** (LIN-4196's `502901c` is the baseline; the eight are LIN-4220, 4223, 4221, 4222, 4224, 4219, 4203 and 4187: `52d2c3d`, `54febbf`, `90bbf82`, `3330526`, `86bde97`, `7d515d3`, `44ab30e`, `d8d186c`). 92 files, +5,993 / -1,442 in all; **outside** `test/` **only 12 files, +177 / -332**: `config.js`, `hook.js`, `opencode-runner.js`, `transcript.js`, `request-usage-flush.js`, `request-usage.js`, `opencode-request-records.js`, `package.json`, plus docs (`README.md`, `docs/testing-and-ci.md`, `docs/module-map.md`, `docs/full-system-test-plan.md`). Most of the test-side movement is the heavy-tier test harness (`stop-group`, `childEnv`, ports, baseline script). `harnesses.js`, `dispatcher.js`, `reapers.js` and `subscription.js` show no diff in the window by `git diff --stat`.
* **The most important thing to verify first: the usage-relay flag moved.** The 11-04 edition's finding `usage-relay-flag-partial` (LOW-MEDIUM, new then) read five record-flush seams (`dispatcher.js:478,1175`, the injected default at `:616`, `reapers.js:1894,3989`) as ignoring `SD_WORKER_USAGE_RELAY`, and listed it under "For John (b)". LIN-4203 (SD `44ab30e` and Harbour `d7ceb373`) now documents `SD_WORKER_USAGE_RELAY` as "the ONE switch for every record flush (Stop, fail, cancel, reap, …)" (`request-usage-flush.js:110`; `config.js:1341-1345`; `hook.js:1823`; `opencode-runner.js:1093`), and removed the snapshot path (`hook.js` -65, `opencode-runner.js` -140, `transcript.js` -111). `dispatcher.js` and `reapers.js` themselves did not change. **Read the code and say whether the five seams are now gated (through** `request-usage-flush.js`**) or still post regardless; whether the row is resolved, improved or unchanged; and whether LIN-4195's "L1 (relay flag off) is closed" statement now matches the source.** Also re-read the contract rows: the two usage calls (`POST /api/dispatch/usage/:itemId`, `POST /api/proxy/runner/usage/:id`) had no row in either contract file at 11-04, and the kit's `[usage]` snapshot post is now gone, so `runner-contract-semantics-cross-repo` and `usage-record-vocabulary-two-readers` (the closed `lane` set in `session-telemetry.js` against the open set in `request-usage-intake.js`) both need a re-read against LIN-4201/4203. `lib/request-usage-intake.js` (+13), `lib/session-telemetry.js` (+15/-) and `routes/dispatch.js` (+8/-) changed in the window; the new `lib/request-usage-vocabulary.js` may be the consolidation of the vocabulary row: check, and do not assume.
* **The previous edition's headline items, to re-ground at HEAD** (it ranked 22 rows; its trend ledger has **121 rows** with a column per edition; carry every row under its stable name, in order, and add a 11-04b column; if a row is retired, say so and say what replaced it):
  1. `resume-model-effort-cross-repo` MEDIUM-HIGH (LIN-4156, Backlog, 0 comments). `lib/dispatch-factory.js`, `lib/follow-up-dispatch.js` and SD `harnesses.js` show no diff in the window by `git diff --stat`.
  2. `credential-decision-multiplicity` MEDIUM-HIGH, borderline at 11-04 (LIN-3822 Backlog). `lib/errors.js` and `lib/workspace.js` show no diff in the window.
  3. `halt-poll-cold-cache-fail-open` MEDIUM (conditional), **ticketed at 11-04 as LIN-4210** (Backlog, 0 comments; behaviour line reads "needs John's ruling", LIN-3024). `lib/poll-halt.js`, `lib/workspace-halt.js` show no diff in the window. The ruling is John's; do not choose an answer and do not re-open the ticket's question.
  4. `runner-contract-semantics-cross-repo` MEDIUM, worsened at 11-04 (Harbour contract 38 rows vs SD 34; four `store` rows unpinned; the two usage calls without a row). LIN-3624 (commented 11-04), LIN-3823 (report-only).
  5. `halt-word-map-copies` MEDIUM (LIN-4157), `home-next-answer-split` MEDIUM (LIN-4158; `lib/home-view.js`, `lib/task-order.js`, `lib/providers/state-map.js` show no diff in the window), `run-page-identity-scrape` MEDIUM, `coherence-loop-stalled` MEDIUM (process; LIN-3449 Todo, 41 children, the 11-03 "parent-all" ruling was applied to the three 11-03 tickets and the six 10-23 children, and the 11-04 edition noted six tickets with no parent: LIN-3823, 3636, 3649, 3843, 3979, 4151).
  6. The new 11-04 rows to re-check, each against its own cited lines: `usage-relay-flag-partial`, `usage-record-vocabulary-two-readers`, `lineage-identity-read-twins` (`lib/founder-lookup.js:34-61` against `lib/dispatch-store.js:1953-1975`; `lib/founder-lookup.js` **is deleted in the window**, so say whether the twin is resolved, moved or relocated), `reap-window-constant-cross-repo`, `task-page-state-outside-owner`, `routes-error-envelope-fragmentation` (`res.status(` count was 275), `cost-fold-partition-restated` (`cost-read.js:63-86`; `cost-read.js` was rewritten by LIN-4201, and `lib/request-usage-fold.js` is new), `vendor-script-list-restated`, `key-state-residue`, `unit-census-convention-split`.
  7. LIN-3490 places-per-decision reading: the 11-04 edition reported its reading under a fixed area guide. **The guide changed in the window**, so this edition's reading is like-for-like only if you run the census at both commits with one guide (the HEAD guide) and say so. Reuse the 11-03 counting rule (excludes sub-rows, resolved, ungraded, informational and process rows).
* **Census tool and the HEAD-guide readings to reproduce.** `scripts/code-shape/census-review.mjs` (documented in `scripts/code-shape/README.md`); the 11-04 edition ran it with the HEAD guide at `5334c81a` against `015aa4c6`, scoped to `^(server\.js$|(lib|routes|public)/.*\.[cm]?js$)`, and read **565 groups / 106** `mustRule` **/ 309 table / 3 gone**. Run it again at `d7ceb373` against `5334c81a` **with one guide for both**, record both full commits and the guide file's hash, and say how the groups moved. The guide edit (LIN-4201) moved files between areas, which can change which groups count as "cross-area", so separate guide effect from code effect exactly as the 11-04 edition did. The 11-04 edition also measured the import graph (493 nodes, 2,026 edges, two SCCs of 6 and 6 with the same members, 0 upward edges, 53 route->route): re-measure it the same way.
* **Follow-ups minted or touched by 11-04, and their state at mint time** (re-check each; `GET $HARBOUR_LOCAL_BASE/api/proxy/issues/<id>`): LIN-4210 (minted 11-04), LIN-4156, LIN-4157, LIN-4158 Backlog; the six 10-23 follow-ups (LIN-3822, 3835, 3836, 1496, 3736, 3624) Backlog; LIN-3823, 3636, 3649, 3843, 3979, 4151 Backlog; LIN-3449 Todo. LIN-4195 In Progress; LIN-4200, 4201, 4203, 4212 Done. **Say by diff, per row, not by assumption**; a file that was touched without being consolidated is a sharper delta than "unchanged". The 11-04 edition's "ticket trend" table is the model for the trend row to add.
* **Report convention:** `docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-YYYY-MM-DD.md` with evidence in `docs/reviews/_evidence-YYYY-MM-DD/` where the previous edition kept it (check). Today's date equals the previous edition's (2026-11-04), so **pick a distinct name** (for example `drift-coherence-review-2026-11-04-run2.md` and `_evidence-2026-11-04-run2/`) and do not overwrite the 11-04 files. PR and commit convention: `LIN-NNNN: <summary> (#PR)`; `ci-success` must be green before merging (`CLAUDE.md`). `lib/periodical-report-gate.js` needs a comment on this task citing a GitHub commit, PR or blob URL, plus the three second-read fields in one comment body, before Done.
* **Siblings and the seams between them.** **Seams & Tangles** (run 6, minted alongside this task; its predecessor `seams-tangles-review-2026-11-04.md`, LIN-4208) owns area-level knots, change coupling and route->route; **Code Quality** (`code-quality-review-2026-11-04.md`, LIN-4207) owns function size; **Stability** (`stability-review-2026-11-04.md`, LIN-4206) owns churn. Read the 11-04 Code Quality and Stability reports for hand-offs to this review. Do not re-flag what they own; cross-link.

## What to do

* **Audit the scope before executing.** Treat the scope above as a starting point to extend, not a checklist to stay inside. Before running the review, look for what is *in-remit but unlisted* and fold it in. Examples to check: the new request-usage modules (`request-usage-fold`, `-loader`, `-vocabulary`, `usage-snapshot-intake`) against the SD side (`request-usage.js`, `request-usage-flush.js`, `opencode-request-records.js`); the legacy-snapshot compatibility that LIN-4203 added to the intake (is "counts legacy snapshots" a second reader of a vocabulary or a deliberate bridge?); the removed runner snapshot path and any comment, doc line or contract row that still describes it (`docs/runner-prompt.md`, SD `docs/module-map.md`); `workspace-kpis-cache.js` as an eighth `lib/*-cache.js` (the `cache-module-family` row said seven); the SD heavy-tier test harness changes (`childEnv`, `stop-group`, ports): new decisions held in more than one place, or a one-owner consolidation worth recording as improved. A scope you could only shrink is suspect; the expected move is to widen it to what the remit actually reaches. Stay **broad in discovery but bounded in output**: the wider scope changes *what you examine*, not *what you report*. The report stays uncapped and severity-ranked (a clean, near-empty result is a genuine outcome), and the follow-up bound below stays as it is.
* **Read prior runs first. This review is trend-aware.** Read the 11-04 report in full (its Headline, Method, Findings, Cross-repo contract verdicts, Sibling hand-offs, Classes and bounds, Follow-ups, For John, Ticket trend, Adversarial second-read and Compact trend ledger), then the 11-03 report as background. Frame every finding as a delta against the 11-04 edition: new, unchanged, improved, worsened or resolved, never a point-in-time snapshot.
* **Run the review.** This review works at the cross-cutting altitude (locally right, globally drifting), distinct from the per-module Code Quality Review; do not re-flag what it owns. Use the repo's own conventions as the reference, introducing no new tooling. Assess: *duplication* (a decision re-implemented where one shared implementation is canonical; coincidental similarity is fine); *convention fragmentation* (competing patterns where one is canonical, flag the outliers); *dependency direction* (imports against the repo's own layering, for example a core module reaching into a route); and the *cross-repo contract* (Harbour <-> SD <-> runner kit). Name the concrete cost a change would hit, not a style preference; no cosmetic churn. Do not find repeated decisions by eye: run the committed census tool (above) at HEAD and at the commit the previous report measured, with one area guide for both runs; record the full commits. Give every `mustRule` group one ruling in a compact table: real (the one place the decision should live and why, or both claimants and your pick), borderline or noise, with a one-line reason; a ruling is your finding, not a question to anyone. List the table groups in one compact table, no ruling. Prose and follow-up tasks only for real groups and for changes since the previous edition. The finding-classes above are **examples, not a limit. Discover the complete set for this remit from the repo; a class list is a floor to build on, never a ceiling to stay inside.**
* **Write an uncapped, trend-framed report.** The deliverable is a clear, severity-ranked report of everything found; finding nothing, one thing or several are all valid; do not pad, cap or invent make-work, and a clean result is a genuine outcome. Ground each finding against the source at HEAD, not prior prose. Close the report with the compact trend ledger: every one of the 121 rows under its stable name, with its severity and its delta against the 11-04 edition, plus any new rows.
* **Mint a bounded set of follow-up tasks: highest-severity only.** Create at most the top \~3 by severity in Linear (fewer is fine; zero is valid when nothing rises to that bar, and in a window this small it usually will). Each is well-scoped: a title, and a description that carries the problem, why it matters, acceptance and file anchors. A fix idea is allowed but goes under an "Unvalidated idea" heading, so later stages treat it as a hypothesis. Leave each in its default state (the 11-04 edition parented its follow-up under LIN-3449 with kind:follow-up; follow that if a ticket is minted). **Before minting, search for an existing ticket already naming the same finding** (the 11-04 edition's "Considered and not minted" list and its search phrases are the model); if one exists, note it in the report instead of minting a duplicate. Record EVERY finding in the report, including the ones not promoted. Err toward under-creating: the Backlog already holds 16 unmoved Drift-family tickets (LIN-4210, 4156, 4157, 4158, the six 10-23 children and the six unparented ones) (`coherence-loop-stalled`), so weigh whether a new ticket will be worked before minting it, and say why.
* **Get a fresh-context adversarial second-read before this task can conclude. This is a required, structural step, not advice.** After the report and any follow-up tasks are written, and before the Done transition, a genuinely separate reader must answer one question cold: *"what is the largest item in this window that this report missed or misfiled?"* **Tier 1 (preferred):** a wholly separate session with no memory of this run. **Tier 2 (accepted fallback):** a fresh-context sub-agent carrying no memory of the report-writing turn. **Tier 3** (this same session re-reading its own report "from a cold stance") **is not accepted**; state which of Tier 1 or Tier 2 you used. Then post **one** comment on this task holding, together in a single body: `Adversarial second-read verdict: AGREE` or `Adversarial second-read verdict: DISAGREE`; `Differed from top finding: YES` or `Differed from top finding: NO` (whether the reader's own answer differed from the report's top-ranked finding, independent of the verdict); and `Disposition: fixed in place`, `Disposition: escalated` or `Disposition: no change`. The engine reads that comment and refuses Done until all three are present in one body. Copy the same three fields into a `## Adversarial Second-Read` section of the report, with the tier, the question and the reader's answer in full. **AGREE and DISAGREE both conclude this task normally. A DISAGREE verdict is itself the escalation**, never a reason to leave this task open.
* **Merge your own report PR.** This task owns it. Once its required CI checks (`ci-success`) are green, merge it before the Done transition. The report is docs-only, so merging it yourself is safe. Only when merging is genuinely impossible (no merge permission, required checks still red) may this task conclude with the PR open, and then only as an explicit handoff naming the blocker in the closing comment. An open report PR is not a normal terminal state.
* **Then conclude this task. Do not leave it open.** Post a concise, severity-ranked summary of the report as a comment on this task, with a link to the merged report (a GitHub commit, PR or blob URL, which the report gate needs). Then move this task to Done. A review task left open is re-recommended indefinitely; the follow-up tasks carry the actionable work forward.
* **Stay review-only.** Producing the report changes no code, config, guide or secrets in either repo, and no docs beyond the report artifact and its evidence. An operator instruction to avoid touching files is about the code and docs *under review*; it does not override this task's own deliverable.

## Drift & Coherence Review 2026-11-04 run 2 (LIN-4232): merged report, second-read gate, summary

**Report (merged):** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/blob/476d9ad478ede67da5cb44195ce24c98d07afa61/docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-04-run2.md
**PR:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2277, squash-merged as `476d9ad478ede67da5cb44195ce24c98d07afa61`. All 7 checks were green on head `1f4de91c` (CI success, Unit tests, E2E 1/4–4/4, Secret scan). Docs-only: the report plus `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-11-04-run2/`.

**Adversarial second-read.** Tier 2: a fresh-context sub-agent with no memory of the writing turns. It formed its own view from the diffs first, then read the report.
- **Question:** "What is the largest item in this window that this report missed or misfiled?"
- **Answer:** LIN-4203's workspace-keyed `usage-snapshot-intake` collection is not in the account-erasure `INVENTORY`, so a Full wipe leaves its documents behind. The completeness guard cannot see a collection opened through a constant with no index spec. LOW-MEDIUM. This was a real miss, verified here and fixed in place as finding #11, and ticketed as LIN-4234.

Adversarial second-read verdict: DISAGREE
Differed from top finding: YES
Disposition: fixed in place

### Summary (severity-ranked; deltas vs the 11-04 edition)

**Window:** LinearViewer `5334c81a..d7ceb373` (8 commits, 4 of them docs-only) and SD `502901c..d8d186c` (8 commits, only one touching production JS). All production movement was in the usage-records cluster and the SD test harness.
- Neither HEAD moved during the review. `origin/main` has since gained LIN-4231 and LIN-4226; those are outside this window.
- An "unchanged" row rests on a zero-line diff of its own cited files. That is high confidence about the code and no information about whether anyone will act on it.

**Findings, ranked:**
1. `resume-model-effort-cross-repo`: MEDIUM-HIGH, unchanged (LIN-4156).
2. `credential-decision-multiplicity`: MEDIUM-HIGH, unchanged (borderline; LIN-3822).

6. `coherence-loop-stalled`: MEDIUM (process), unchanged. New datum: LIN-4214 went stale behind code fixed under LIN-4203.

10. `cache-module-family`: LOW, **worsened**. 8 caches; a second keyed stale-while-revalidate cache repeats the LIN-2798 clear race.
11. `usage-snapshot-prose-residue`: LOW, **new**. Text still describes the retired `[usage]` snapshot as live: one user-visible string, one agent-catalog line, two doc lines, and comments.
12. `completeness-precedence-restated`: borderline, **new**, not graded.
- **Resolved:**
  - `usage-relay-flag-partial`: SD now checks the flag once, at `request-usage-flush.js:114`. Residual: LIN-4214 has no per-seam flag-off test for fail, cancel or stall, and the posters are exported ungated.
  - `lineage-identity-read-twins`: one store query.
  - `cost-fold-partition-restated`: one `countedRowsOf`.

**Counts:**

- Census under one guide (HEAD `areas.json`, sha256 `e3194f52`): 566 / 106 / 307 / 1, with 0 `mustRule` groups moving. Rulings: 34 real, 30 borderline, 42 noise.

- **Ledger: 124 rows** (121 carried + 3 new; none retired).

**Follow-ups:**

- Dated evidence comments on **LIN-4214** (what LIN-4203 landed against its acceptance) and **LIN-2798** (the second cache with the same race).
